newsitem.title: CHINA: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - April 3.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Chinese newspapers - April 3.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Chinese political and business stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Beijing. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (8610) 6532-1921. Fax: (8610) 6532-4978.
PEOPLE'S DAILY
- President Jiang Zemin meets San Francisco Mayor Willie Brown and praises Brown's efforts for promoting friendly ties and cooperation between China and the United States.
- Premier Li Peng and Thai Prime Minister Chavalit Yongchaiyudh hold talks in Beijing, agreeing that China and Thailand should forge closer ties and cooperation.
FINANCIAL NEWS
- The People's Insurance Company of China (PICC) Life pays 171 million yuan into PICC Reinsurance. PICC Property pays 1.29 billion yuan.
- The Bank of China Trust & Consultancy Co changes its name to China Orient Trust & Investment Co.
- Xinhua Life Insurance Co premium income hits 380 million yuan by the end of February after six months of operation.
- The State Administration of Foreign Exchange issues a foreign exchange license to Huatai Property Insurance Co Ltd.
- An official survey finds 38.3 percent of Chinese consumers choose investment in treasury bonds.
CHINA SECURITIES
- An editorial says the central bank should not yet cut the bank reserve ratio because policy makers need to consider the impact on the stock markets.
- Gross industrial output of China's rubber industry hits 46.5 billion yuan in 1996.
ECONOMIC DAILY
- Prices of domestic steel products are seen rebounding in 1997.
CHINA BUSINESS TIMES
- A Ministry of Finance official says China plans to levy a social security tax to boost collection of social security funds.
CHINA DAILY
- Chinese television maker Sichuan Changhong Electric Appliances Co Ltd sees sales of 10.7 billion yuan in 1996, becoming China's top electronics firm in terms of turnover.
- All coal mining companies will be required to buy accidental-injury insurance for their employees after July 1.
